rows.b: Transistors made from rolled sheets of carbon atoms, thinner and potentially faster than silicon channels. Whole tiny computers have been built from them in labs.
Instead of one giant chip, several small specialized chips are bonded together in one package and act as one processor. Each chiplet does what it does best.
Photonic chips that move data as light sit in the same package as the electronic chips that think. Data flies between them at light speed with little heat.
Clouds of atoms chilled to near absolute zero mimic the quantum behavior of materials and molecules. Instead of calculating nature, the machine becomes a small piece of it.
Two thousand vacuum tubes processed punched tape at high speed to find the settings of an enemy cipher machine. It compared patterns statistically and printed its scores for analysts.
Sixty-four kilobytes of memory, famous sound and sprite graphics, and a huge game library. It became the best-selling single computer model of all time.
A few clever CPU cores direct thousands of simple GPU cores, splitting every job by talent. This pairing powers gaming, AI, and science computing.
A future chip that lives in the fridge beside qubits, translating room-temperature commands into the delicate pulses qubits need. Near-term: prototypes exist in labs.
